target_claim: If a prime ideal \(\mathfrak p\mid p\) divides \((n+\alpha)\mathfrak a\) and the rational prime \(p\) is unramified, then \(p\) splits completely in the splitting field \(L\) of the minimal polynomial of \(\alpha\).
source_quote: Moreover there are no primes $\mathfrak{p}\mid p$ such that $\mathfrak{p}\mid (n+\alpha)\mathfrak{a}$, $p$ is not ramified and $p$ doesn't split completely in $L$.
